newsitem.title: USA: Most Bridgestone/Firestone workers recalled - USW. [CORRECTED 18:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Most Bridgestone/Firestone workers recalled - USW. [CORRECTED 18:50 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects union name in headline from UAW to USW.)

Labeling it a victory, the United Steelworkers union said Thursday that Bridgestone/Firestone Inc, the U.S. arm of Japanese tire maker Bridgestone Corp, has recalled virtually all union workers who struck the company two years ago.

But union members are working under contract terms offered by the company before the strike began and the USW will continue its "corporate campaign" against Bridgestone/Firestone until a new agreement is reached and fired workers are rehired, union officials said.
The USW's rubber/plastics division held a conference this week in Pittsburgh and officials made their comments at a news conference.
The USW merged with the former United Rubber Workers union in July 1995, a year after rubber workers launched a 4,000 member strike against Nashville-based Bridgestone/Firestone.

"As a result of our escalating campaign, the company in the last two weeks escalated its recall of the strikers...Virtually all of them have been notified to return to work," said John Sellers, executive vice president of the rubber/plastics conference.
However, Sellers said up to 150 workers remain off their jobs because they were fired on "strike-related charges."
"Those who are back on the job are working without the protection of a contract...what this all means is that while our campaign is working, it is far from finished."
Sellers said the union will augment its so-called "Don't Buy" campaign against Bridgestone/Firestone to pressure it to the bargaining table. There are no contract talks scheduled.
The union's campaign has targeted car dealers, tire distributors and consumers seeking a boycott of Bridgestone/Firestone products.
Earlier this year, the Saturn division of General Motors Corp said it would allow customers to have Bridgestone tires on their new Saturns replaced with another brand at the company's expense.
Sellers said the union also will step up its media campaign by distributing more negative material about the company.
Rubber workers struck the company in July 1994 after negotiations failed to produce a new contract. The company then hired replacement workers in January 1995.
The union offered an unconditional return to work in May 1995, ending the strike.
Workers were recalled periodically for several months but are working under contract provisions offered by the company before the strike began.
